## 1. What this map is, and what it is not

- **171 objectives.** One objective is one statutory statement of the national curriculum maths programme of study for Years 3 to 6 (Year 3: 33, Year 4: 42, Year 5: 47, Year 6: 49). Its wording is the Department for Education's, quoted verbatim.
- **Sourced, and ours, are kept apart.**
  - **Sourced (DfE):** the objective id, year group, strand and the statement text, and where it is located (§2).
  - **Our instructional choices:** the learner outcome, prerequisite knowledge, vocabulary, examples, proposed mastery evidence, the mapping to islands and skills, and the coverage judgement. None of these is claimed to be in the programme of study.
- **Year allocation is verified against the official source, not inferred from island labels** (§2.2). It also carries a caveat the source states itself (§2.2): schools need only teach the programme by the end of the key stage.
- **Statutory and 11+ are separate.** §6 lists extension candidates. The 11+ has **no single official specification** (§6), so no extension item has an official source, and none is labelled as required by any 11+ test.
- **Mastery thresholds are not set here.** The mastery evidence says *what kind* of evidence would show the objective is secure. How many items, and what threshold, is owned by MAST-001 (CUR-002 §4.3).
- **Coverage is a desk judgement.** "Addressed", "partial" and "not addressed" compare each statement with the **titles and descriptions** of the existing skills and lessons. Nobody reviewed the question content for this map. For Fractions that review is CUR-004. For other islands it comes with R4. Only the Fractions island (`fractions.*`) is the R1 product; the 18 other islands are unaccepted previews (D-001).
- This is **mapping and review**, not implementation. Gaps in §7 are inputs to later releases, not defects.

### 2.2 Year allocation

The programme of study is set out **year by year**, and each statement's year is the year of the section it sits in. The same source also says (verbatim, under *School curriculum*):

> The programmes of study for mathematics are set out year-by-year for key stages 1 and 2. Schools are, however, only required to teach the relevant programme of study by the end of the key stage. Within each key stage, schools therefore have the flexibility to introduce content earlier or later than set out in the programme of study. In addition, schools can introduce key stage content during an earlier key stage, if appropriate. All schools are also required to set out their school curriculum for mathematics on a year-by-year basis and make this information available online.

So a year group here is the programme's own sequence, **not a requirement to teach in that year**: the statutory duty is by the end of the key stage (Year 4 for lower KS2, Year 6 for upper KS2). Product recommendations by year are our choice (PARENT-001). One statement in the key stage 2 introduction does fix a year: pupils should have memorised their multiplication tables up to and including 12 × 12 **by the end of Year 4**. (The Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check is described in the backlog's TT epic; its official guidance was not verified for this map.)

**The island labels were checked, not trusted** (§4.3). Where an island's `years` disagree with the statutory years of the objectives it covers, the table says so.

## 3. Proposed mastery evidence, by kind

Each objective names one or more kinds. Every kind assumes the CUR-002 §4 contract: **independent** means first attempt, no hint, answer not revealed, a fresh item. How many items count, and the threshold, belong to MAST-001.

| Kind | Proposed evidence |
|---|---|
| **F** Fluency and recall | Independent, first-attempt answers to **mixed** (not sequential) items, with no hint and no revealed answer, re-checked after a gap (spaced), including the related facts or the inverse. |
| **R** Representation and concept | Independent identification or use of the idea across **at least two representations**, including one not used in teaching. |
| **P** Procedure | Independent completion of **fresh** calculations by the method, each checked by an inverse operation or an estimate. |
| **X** Reasoning and explanation | Independent justification, explanation or counterexample, using the lesson's sentence frames or the learner's own words (CUR-003 reflection rules). |
| **W** Problems in context | Independent solution of **unfamiliar** contextual problems where the learner chooses the operation, with transfer to a new context. |
| **V** Vocabulary, reading and writing | Independent reading, writing or naming across varied cases, including edge cases (for example zero as a place holder). |

**Reading this table.**
- The island teaches 8 objectives, all from the Number: fractions strand (Y3.FRAC.2, Y3.FRAC.3, Y3.FRAC.4, Y3.FRAC.6, Y3.FRAC.7, Y4.FRAC.1, Y4.FRAC.3, Y5.FRAC.2).
- Not taught by the R1 island, although they are Year 3–5 fractions objectives: **adding and subtracting fractions** (Y3.FRAC.5, Y4.FRAC.4, Y5.FRAC.4), **fractions greater than 1 and mixed numbers** (Y5.FRAC.3), **comparison with different denominators** (Y5.FRAC.1) and **tenths and hundredths as decimals** (Y3.FRAC.1, Y4.FRAC.2). Whether R1 should include any of them is a Product Owner decision (§8).
- `fractions.fraction-of` needs division facts (Y3.MD.1, Y4.MD.1). CUR-002 makes this a "best after" recommendation, never a lock (D-019).

## 6. Optional 11+ extension (AC2)

**There is no single official 11+ specification.** The 11+ is set by individual grammar schools, local authorities and consortia, using providers such as GL Assessment or CEM, and its content and format vary by area and provider. The sources I found while building this map were commercial or anecdotal and disagreed on how far 11+ maths reaches into Year 6; I could not find an exam provider's own specification. The backlog's own rule applies: do not describe all 11+ exams as one uniform syllabus (backlog §3). Verified exam profiles belong to EXAM-001 and EXAM-002 (R5).

So this section lists only **extension candidates**: things the existing islands teach that go **beyond the statutory wording**. They are our instructional choices. They have **no official source**, and none is claimed to be required by any 11+ test.

| Id | Candidate | Related statutory objectives | Maps to | Mastery evidence | Why it is an extension candidate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E11.1 | Ratio notation (a : b), simplifying ratios and sharing an amount in a ratio. Example: Share £40 in the ratio 3 : 5 | Y6.RP.1; Y6.RP.4 | `ratio-algebra.ratio` | **W** Problems in context | The statutory Year 6 ratio and proportion statements do not use ratio notation (Y6.RP.1, Y6.RP.4); the island teaches it. No official source: 11+ content varies by area and provider (EXAM-001, EXAM-002); whether any named 11+ test needs it is unverified. |
| E11.2 | Finding the nth term of a linear sequence. Example: Nth term of 5, 8, 11, 14 is 3n + 2 | Y6.ALG.2 | `ratio-algebra.sequences` | **R** Representation and concept | The statutory text is 'generate and describe linear number sequences' (Y6.ALG.2); a formula for the nth term is not stated. No official source: 11+ content varies by area and provider (EXAM-001, EXAM-002); whether any named 11+ test needs it is unverified. |
| E11.3 | Solving two-step equations. Example: 3n + 4 = 19 | Y6.ALG.3 | `ratio-algebra.equations` | **P** Procedure | The statutory text expresses missing-number problems algebraically (Y6.ALG.3); solving two-step equations is not stated. No official source: 11+ content varies by area and provider (EXAM-001, EXAM-002); whether any named 11+ test needs it is unverified. |
| E11.4 | Working backwards to find a starting number. Example: 'I think of a number, double it and add 3. The answer is 17.' | Y6.ASMD.8 | `problem-solving.backwards` | **W** Problems in context + **X** Reasoning and explanation | A problem-solving technique, not a statutory statement (related: Y6.ASMD.8). No official source: 11+ content varies by area and provider (EXAM-001, EXAM-002); whether any named 11+ test needs it is unverified. |
| E11.5 | Bar-model puzzles: sum and difference, and 'times as many'. Example: 'A is 3 times B and together they are 48' | Y3.MD.3; Y6.RP.1 | `problem-solving.sum-difference` | **W** Problems in context + **R** Representation and concept | A representation and technique, not a statutory statement (related: Y3.MD.3, Y6.RP.1). No official source: 11+ content varies by area and provider (EXAM-001, EXAM-002); whether any named 11+ test needs it is unverified. |

Example: Turn from north to east: a quarter turn clockwise | Y3.GPS.2 | `shapes-angles.turns` | **V** Vocabulary, reading and writing | Not in the maths programme of study (compass work is in other subjects); the island includes it. No official source: 11+ content varies by area and provider (EXAM-001, EXAM-002); whether any named 11+ test needs it is unverified. |

The `mock-exams` island ("11+ style") is exam technique and format practice, not curriculum content. It is deliberately **not** used as evidence that any statutory objective is covered.

Objectives **not addressed** by any existing skill, grouped by strand. These are inputs to R4 (curriculum expansion), not R1 defects.

|---|---|
| Measurement | Y3.MEAS.1, Y5.MEAS.1, Y5.MEAS.2, Y5.MEAS.5, Y6.MEAS.1, Y6.MEAS.3, Y6.MEAS.6, Y6.MEAS.7 |
| Geometry: properties of shapes | Y3.GPS.4, Y4.GPS.3, Y4.GPS.4, Y5.GPS.3, Y6.GPS.1, Y6.GPS.4 |
| Number: place value | Y4.NPV.9, Y5.NPV.6 |
| Number: multiplication and division | Y5.MD.2, Y5.MD.3, Y5.MD.8 |
| Number: fractions (including decimals and percentages) | Y5.FRAC.7, Y6.FRAC.4, Y6.FRAC.5, Y6.FRAC.8, Y6.FRAC.9 |
| Number: addition, subtraction, multiplication and division | Y6.ASMD.2, Y6.ASMD.6 |
| Algebra | Y6.ALG.4 |

**Totals:** 27 not addressed, 69 partial, 75 addressed, of 171. Topics with nothing taught: measuring and converting length, mass and capacity, volume, symmetry, circles, primes, squares and cubes, order of operations, Roman numerals, long division, fraction multiplication and division, and measuring angles with a protractor.

## 9. Checks and maintenance

`src/curriculum/map.test.ts` runs with `npm test` and checks that:
- every Year 3–6 statutory statement in the extracted source is in the map exactly once, with the right year, strand, anchor and position;
- every objective has every required field, a valid mastery kind and existing prerequisite ids, never from a later year, with no cycles;
- every mapped skill exists, "not addressed" objectives map to nothing, and the R1 "taught" objectives map to Fractions skills;
- extension candidates are separate, carry no source and are never labelled statutory;
- the island snapshot matches the live islands, so the map is flagged when islands change;
- this document lists every objective, and contains no invented mastery threshold.

To update: edit [`curriculum-map.csv`](curriculum-map.csv), then run `python3 -I docs/product/verification/build-curriculum-map-doc.py`. If the DfE page changes, rerun the extractor, review the diff, and update the map.
